items.statement: Revenue mix: India 88%, international 12%; order book mix: India 96%, international 4%. BSNL 4G dominates.
items.quote: From a revenue mix, India was 88% compared to the international revenues of 12%. And from an order book mix, 96% of India and 4% of international.

items.statement: BSNL milestone collections to reduce receivables significantly in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: We have met the milestone delivery requirements. And this is the quarter when we will see a significant amount of collections coming from BSNL.

items.statement: No explicit fund-raising plans mentioned; cost optimization (Project Sanchay) delivering INR13 cr in Q2, INR23 cr in H1.
items.quote: "Project Sanchay continued to deliver results, generating savings of approximately INR13 crores during the quarter and approximately INR23 crores for H1."

items.statement: FY27 ROA guidance may be overshot due to strong asset growth, stable asset quality, and lower-than-expected opex.
items.quote: Considering these outcomes, we could overshoot our guided ROA range. We remain vigilant of revised monetary stance, risk of global rates and supply chain disruptions, coupled with weather-induced issues.

items.statement: Secured loan book target for FY27 is 56% of total advances (up from 52% in Q2 FY27).
items.quote: We already mentioned earlier minimum we'll try 56% as the secured percentage. And every year, we have said we will improve it by 5%.

items.statement: Opex to ATA ratio expected at 6.2% (vs. guided 6.4%), saving ~0.2% due to lower-than-expected spends.
items.quote: Now coming to the opex, I think we had given an indication last time that it will be around opex to ATA ratio of 6.4%. Now considering the way it is moving, we feel it may end up at 6.2%.

items.statement: NIM expected at ~8.35% for H2 FY27 (down 10 bps from Q2 FY27 due to rate hike).
items.quote: So we feel the margin would come down to around 8.35% for the second half of the year. Now coming to the mix change, yes, whatever is the impact will be set off by planned DA, which we are planning.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at ~6.9% in Q2 FY27; expected to rise post-Q1 rate hikes.
items.quote: We benefited from the downward repricing of deposits, which helped maintain the cost of funds at around 6.9%. Although no rate hikes were taken in Q2, the increase effective in Q1 would now start showing, and we expect the cost of funds to start moving upwards.

items.statement: Microfinance demand strong; new customer acquisition added 2 lakh in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: New customer acquisition increased sequentially with an addition of 2 lakh customers in Q2. Despite usual weather disruptions in July, August, September, we have delivered on healthy disbursements and collections

items.statement: MSME demand robust; disbursements grew 44% YoY in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: MSME business built upon the capacities created and product changes grew to INR3,871 crores, up 51.3% year-on-year. The new book reached INR3,000 crores plus while maintaining GNPA of 0.5

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected to be mid-teen to high-teen % (vs. H1 20% YoY). EBITDA margin ~12% for FY27.
items.quote: I think it's very difficult for me to hazard a guess what's going to happen in the second half. But I think our initial assessment of 12%, 14%, I think we should do a between mid-teen to a little high-teen numbers for the year-end.

items.statement: CAPEX of ~Rs. 50-75 crore planned for H2 FY27, primarily for pharma, aroma, hydrogenation, and biosurfactant expansions.
items.quote: I think we'll have another about between Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 70 crore, Rs. 75 crore of spend that will happen in the second half. And then I think nothing beyond that.

items.statement: No significant CAPEX beyond FY27 until Saudi Arabia project approvals finalized.
items.quote: Going forward, I think over the next year, at least we will not have any significant CAPEX spend. And then we'll, of course, look at KSA, which will be the new area.

items.statement: Export revenue contribution expected to reach 30%+ of total revenue by FY27-end (up from 27% in H1 FY27).
items.quote: Our first target, I think by the end of this year should be that at least 30% plus of our revenue should come from export.

items.statement: Export growth driven by HPPC (personal care, oil & gas) and textile segments, with focus on Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America.
items.quote: We saw broad-based growth in the export side. Within the HPPC, I think personal care was one of the key drivers, if you compare it on a Y-o-Y basis. And then also some of the new segments like oil and gas also saw some traction in this quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin compression in core B2B due to freight costs (doubled/tripled YoY) and raw material price hikes, partially offset by product mix shift.
items.quote: The expenses on freight have significantly impacted in the current year. Even though our exports have grown significantly, the freight costs have almost doubled, tripled over what they were in the first half of last year or Q2 of last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stabilize at ~12% for FY27, with improvements anticipated in FY28+ due to pharma/aroma ramp-up.
items.quote: This year, we will be at similar kind of EBITDA of around 12% plus/minus. That is what for this year is our take. And as I said, some of these initiatives are still work in progress.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement expected from pharma/aroma segments (higher-margin products), but pharma ramp-up is slow (6-24 months for approvals).
items.quote: Hopefully, we will get the approvals now going over the next couple of quarters. And then yes, as I said, as these segments like pharma, aroma, you know, start becoming a significant part of the overall business, we should see steady gross margin improvement.

items.statement: Cautious customer buying behavior due to geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East) and raw material volatility; H2 FY27 demand outlook uncertain.
items.quote: the global market, the situation is changing so rapidly. We are not able to know whether we'll be able to ship our shipments through Bab e l-Mandeb or through Hormuz, or the insurance and the freights are going up

items.statement: Shift to higher-margin products (pharma excipients, personal care, oil & gas) and rationalization of low-margin products (e.g., B2C tail-cutting).
items.quote: The focus has been on a very prudent product mix where higher-margin products are being sold in the export, but also in the domestic market. We have had a rationalization by tail cutting.

items.statement: Key risks: geopolitical tensions (Middle East), freight/logistics volatility, raw material price swings, and slow pharma approval cycles.
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East kept pressure on freight and logistics and customers across several end -user industries rema in cautious in their buying

items.statement: Animal Health & Nutrition (AHN) demand peaks in Q3-Q4 FY27; Q2 FY27 was seasonally weak.
items.quote: Generally, the second quarter is the weakest for the AHN division. The third and fourth quarters will peak.

items.statement: FY27 disbursements to surpass FY26 levels (~INR35,000 crore non-IR disbursements in FY26).
items.quote: the guidance that we have given is that, in FY27 also, we will surpass disbursement that we did last FY, and that guidance remains intact.

items.statement: AUM target of INR5,00,000 crore intact for FY27 end, likely achieved by Q3.
items.quote: we stand by the target of reaching near about INR5,00,000 crores, maybe more than that, maybe 1,000 or 2,000 possible shortfall but the target is fully intact for end of FY27.

items.statement: Pipeline includes metros, ports, renewable energy, thermal power, Gencos, and road linkages.
items.quote: In H2, you will find that we will be lending to metros, ports, renewable energy, thermal power, Gencos that have linkages with the Railways. We will be lending to few road linkages also.

items.statement: Non-IR margins 2-3.5x higher than Railways (1.3% NIM). FY26 non-IR disbursements: INR35,000 crore.
items.quote: Whatever non-IR business that we are garnering, margin is atleast 2 times or 3 times and 3.5 times high. So, what will happen that even if my AUM growth is not growing very high, it may not be growing in double digits, but my PAT will always be growing near to double

items.statement: Railways capex risks managed via multilateral partnerships (World Bank, others).
items.quote: are kind of being the sole financing arm of Indian Railways and, playing the role as aggregators, we are already talking to World Bank, other multilaterals, as well as domestic players

items.statement: Bank of America to invest ~Rs. 18,000 crore in Jio Credit (subject to approvals)
items.quote: The transaction, which is subject to regulatory approvals, is expected to bring around Rs. 18,000 crore in growth capital.

items.statement: Bank of America to infuse ~Rs. 9,500 crore into Jio Credit (subject to approvals)
items.quote: The infusion of the first tranche of its investment of around Rs. 9,500 crore from Bank of America into Jio Credit Limited, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals, will further bolster our capital base.

items.statement: Jio Credit’s Gross Assets Under Management (AUM) grew 154% YoY to Rs. 37,320 crore
items.quote: Jio Credit’s Gross Assets Under Management rose to Rs. 37,320 crore as of September 30, 2026, representing a 154% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Jio Credit’s gross disbursements reached Rs. 13,135 crore (98% YoY growth)
items.quote: During the quarter, gross disbursements reached a new all-time high of Rs. 13,135 crore, representing a 98% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank’s customer deposit base expanded to Rs. 643 crore (53% YoY growth)
items.quote: Jio Payments Bank expanded its customer deposit base to Rs. 643 crore, up 53% year-on-year across 40 lakh CASA accounts.

items.statement: Jio Payments Solutions’ Total Payment Value (TPV) stood at Rs. 14,682 crore
items.quote: At Jio Payment Solutions, Total Payment Value, or TPV, stood at Rs. 14,682 crore.

items.statement: Jio Payments Solutions’ net processing margin increased to 14 basis points
items.quote: Our net processing margin increased to 14 basis points in Q2 FY27, up from 9 basis points in Q2 FY26 and 12 basis points in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Jio Credit’s Net Interest Income grew 116% YoY to Rs. 302 crore
items.quote: Net Interest Income grew 116% year-on-year to Rs. 302 crore, and up sequentially from Rs. 257 crore in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Jio Credit’s Pre-Provisioning Operating Profit surged 151% YoY to Rs. 201 crore
items.quote: Pre-Provisioning Operating Profit surged 151% year-on-year to Rs. 201 crore, and up from Rs. 154 crore in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Jio Credit’s Profit After Tax increased 140% YoY to Rs. 120 crore
items.quote: Profit After Tax increased 140% year-on-year from Rs. 220 crore, and up from Rs. 96 crore in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank’s average cost of borrowing stable at 7.08% (excluding TREPS)
items.quote: Our average cost of borrowing, excluding TREPS, stood at 7.08% in Q2 FY27, compared to 7.07% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: JioFinance app reached 3.2 crore unique users
items.quote: The JioFinance app, our primary digital storefront for our retail offerings, clocked 3.2 crore unique users across all digital properties.

items.statement: JioBlackRock AMC’s AUM grew 57% YoY to Rs. 22,746 crore
items.quote: JioBlackRock AMC saw its Closing AUM reach Rs. 22,746 crore, growing 57% year-on-year and 24% sequentially.

items.statement: Jio Payments Solutions’ TPV shift to margin-accretive merchant segments
items.quote: The quarter-on-quarter adjustment in TPV was a deliberate outcome of our strategic pivot 2 towards margin-accretive merchant

items.statement: Jio Credit’s loan book anchored in secured lending and high-rated corporate exposures
items.quote: Our primary focus remains squarely on disciplined, risk-calibrated growth. We continue to build a high-quality loan book anchored entirely in secured lending segments and high-rated corporate exposures.

items.statement: Jio Credit’s total borrowings stood at Rs. 42,000 crore (250% YoY growth)
items.quote: Total borrowings stood at a little over Rs. 42,000 crore, representing a 250% year-on-year growth and up sequentially from Rs. 28,120 crore in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Management reaffirms FY27 AUM growth guidance of 20-25% despite flat gold prices, citing tonnage expansion.
items.quote: we will give a AUM growth of about 20% to 25% for the year. And the ROE, you might see because of the numbers that we have given in Q2 and Q1, there might be an upside to the guidance that we have already given.

items.statement: Targeting ROA of 3% and ROE of 18% by FY27 end, with Q2 ROE at 17% and ROA at 2.8%.
items.quote: That is the objective, and we want to keep it steady at that, being a franchise which is predictable and trying to get a 3% ROA and ROE has been what we had envisioned about 2 years ago.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth expected to continue in H2 FY27, with Q3/Q4 seasonality driving higher disbursements.
items.quote: Our seasonality is more in Q3 and Q4. So you will see that happening as we go forward. We already have an IGL product. We have been operating with it in Q2 also.

items.statement: Gold loan disbursements grew 31% YoY to INR5,822 crore in Q2 FY27, with AUM at INR11,917 crore.
items.quote: our gold loan business continued its growth trajectory. Disbursements stood at INR5,822 crores, a growth of 31% Y -o-Y. And the gold AUM grew 77% Y -o-Y to INR11,917 crores

items.statement: Total disbursements grew 28% YoY to INR6,676 crore in Q2 FY27, with AUM at INR22,035 crore.
items.quote: Our total disbursements grew 28% Y - o-Y to INR6,676 crores, and our AUM grew 37% Y-o-Y to INR22,035 crores

items.statement: Gold loan yields stable at 16.4% in Q2 FY27 despite competitive pressure, with 10 bps drop YoY.
items.quote: Our overall yield on the core loan book remained constant in quarter 2 compared to quarter 1 at 16.40 levels. The optical increase in yield by 29 bps is because the last quarter had a higher DA unwinding impact.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowing flat at 7.8% in Q2 FY27, with 33% fixed-rate borrowings and 24% MCLR-linked.
items.quote: Our weighted average cost of borrowing for quarter 2, flat at the same level as the previous 3 quarters at 7.80. This is represented in the funding profile slide in the deck.

items.statement: Direct assignments of INR700 crore in gold loans to deleverage, improving debt-equity ratio to 4.6% from 4.9%.
items.quote: We did direct assignments of approximately INR700 crores of the gold loan book to deleverage. This aided by higher co-lending in the gold portfolio, helped in bringing down the debt-equity ratio from 4.9% to 4.6

items.statement: Q3-Q4 FY27 commercial vehicle volumes expected to be stronger than Q2 FY27, with H2 historically 20% higher than H1.
items.quote: Based on our current indication, we expect Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than Q2. Overall volumes and historically also H2 is always 20% up on H1.

items.statement: Q3-Q4 FY27 agri segment demand expected to remain consistent, supported by lower tractor inventory levels.
items.quote: Demand in the Agri segment has remained consistent. We expect this momentum to continue into Q3, supported by relatively lower inventory levels of tractors in the market.

items.statement: Q3-Q4 FY27 trailer axle production to shift fully to extruded beam process, improving cost competitiveness.
items.quote: By Q3 or Q4, we will be producing our trailer axles in this methodology only by the extruded beam process.

items.statement: Q3-Q4 FY27 price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1 customers expected to offset rising consumable and commodity costs.
items.quote: The price revisions, including concluded with the OEMs and Tier 1 customers are expected to support us during the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Q3-Q4 FY27 capacity utilization of seamless tube facility to improve progressively, supporting margins.
items.quote: We expect our utilization levels to improve progressively over the coming 2 quarters. This should further support our margins as well.

items.statement: FY27 tipping jack volumes to reach 50-60% of 800-unit capacity by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: We've set a capacity of close to 800 numbers. We should be at at least 50%, 60% of that capacity by quarter 4.

items.statement: INR120 crores spent on seamless tube facility capex (INR60 crores internal accruals + INR50 crores term loan) by Q2 FY27.
items.quote: our own contribution is about INR60 crores, okay, INR60 crores plus INR50 crores -- INR70 crores, we have taken as our -- from the term loan, INR70 crores plus INR50 crores, INR120 crores out of the INR170 crores

items.statement: Q3-Q4 FY27 commercial vehicle demand robust, with OEMs indicating stronger volumes than Q2 FY27.
items.quote: The momentum in the commercial segment has continued with robust demand indicated by the OEMs. Based on our current indication, we expect Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than

items.statement: Management confirms FY27 EBITDA guidance of mid-to-high teens, despite H1 overperformance.
items.quote: we definitely stay true on the guidance, that yes, H1 has been far stronger than the guidance and we expect the trends to continue but definitely mid-to-high teens (EBITDA) for the balance of the year is something that we are anchored towards.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 RevPAR growth expected to be double-digit, driven by events and festive demand.
items.quote: we are very much on track for double-digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

items.statement: Total capex for 5 owned projects (Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh) is ₹1,432 cr.
items.quote: the capex for our five contracted pipelines, is Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh is around INR1,432 crores.

items.statement: ₹450 cr capex spent by FY27-end, ₹600 cr in FY28 for the 5 owned projects.
items.quote: By the end of this year, we will be spending around INR450 crores. Next year, we are looking at spending around INR600 crores.

items.statement: BKC Mumbai project capex remains ₹800 cr (₹400 cr equity, ₹400 cr debt).
items.quote: There is no change in the overall capex cost as of now. The INR 800 crores of our committed capex remains the same.

items.statement: Corporate rate negotiations targeting mid-to-high double-digit growth for CY27.
items.quote: we are pitching for mid-to-high double-digit growth rates in terms of our ask rates.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 46% (up 118 bps YoY) due to pricing discipline and cost efficiency.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin of 46%, a 118-basis point improvement over the previous year.

items.statement: EBITDA flow-through ~60% excluding ESOP and Coorg ramp-up costs.
items.quote: If you adjust these just two impacts, our flow-through will be close to 60, which is industry-leading flow-through to margins.

items.statement: Corporate pricing shifted to dynamic rates (60-70% of static rates) for higher yield.
items.quote: we pivoted almost 60% to 70% of our static rates on corporate to dynamic rates. And we also over -index on the GDS bookings

items.statement: Domestic demand robust (30% YoY growth in Q2), international demand slowly reviving.
items.quote: Domestic demand continued to Leela Palaces Hotels & demonstrate robust growth, and international demand also returned in strength

items.statement: Events (MICE, weddings) driving demand across cities and resorts; occupancy headroom remains.
items.quote: Events are a common thread across both corporate MICE, underpins weekday business in our cities, while weddings and social celebrations bring demand to our cities and resorts throughout the year

items.statement: FY27 growth guidance revised to 26-27% (vs earlier 20-25%) for full year; medium-term 20-25% maintained.
items.quote: I would say FY27, two quarters gone. We're seeing the early onset of festival first 9, 10 days. I would say probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis.

items.statement: New loans guidance for FY27: 60-62 million (vs 13.5M in Q2).
items.quote: We are well on track to deliver between 60 million to 62 million new loans in FY27.

items.statement: Customer additions guidance for FY27: 18-20 million (vs 4.42M in Q2).
items.quote: We are clear about adding between 18 MM to 20 MM customers to the franchise in FY27.

items.statement: Opex-to-NTI improvement target: 25-40 bps for FY27 despite investments in gold loan branches, MFI, and tech.
items.quote: We remain pretty comfortable place to deliver a 25 to 40 basis point improvement in FY27 on opex-to-NTI.

items.statement: MSME growth: 3% in Q2; expects double-digit growth in H2 FY27.
items.quote: MSME grew by 3%. It should now start to grow actually. So , we should start to see as we get in the second half, a double -digit kind of growth momentum in the business

items.statement: 3PL (3+ loans) origination reduced from 14% to 7%; target 3.5% in 6 months.
items.quote: have brought that down from 14% to 7% in terms of origination my mandate to the team is to bring that down to 3.5 % in the 6 months' time

items.statement: Retail loan growth accelerating; Q2 FY27 disbursements crossed Rs 90,000 cr vs Rs 76,000 cr in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The pace of retail disbursements is accelerating and has cro ssed Rs 90,000 crores during Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1 of this year

items.statement: Retail assets (ex-agri) annual growth at 11.2% (Sept '26) vs 9.1% (June '26) and 7.4% (March '26).
items.quote: loan book, especially for retail assets ex agri, September'26 annual growth is about 11.2% compared to 9.1% as of June'26 and 7.4% as of March'26.

items.statement: MSME/mid-market loan growth at 23.5% YoY (Sept '26) vs 17-18% in prior quarters; ECLGS 5.0 scheme boosted disbursals.
items.quote: MSME and mid-market business, growth momentum is also improving rapidly. September'26 EOP loan growth has grown 23.5 % year -on-year compared to 17% to 18% year-on-year growth levels seen in the last few quarters

items.statement: New credit card issuances grew 19% QoQ to 1.4 million.
items.quote: New credit card issuances at 1.4 million have grown by nearly 19% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Retail consumption robust (passenger vehicles, 2-wheelers up >30% YoY; consumer durables +11% YoY).
items.quote: Retail consumption growth has also been robust with passenger vehicles, 2-wheeler sales all growing upwards of 30-plus percentage. Even consumer durables grew at about 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Economic momentum strong: GDP growth better than anticipated; industrial production, e-way bills, cargo activity, credit growth reflect sustained momentum.
items.quote: GDP growth in Q2 FY27 has been better than anticipated and high performance indicators such as industrial production, strong e-way bill, cargo activity, credit growth reflects sustained momentum.

items.statement: Agri asset quality stable; GNPA unchanged YoY (Sept '26 vs June '26); sowing area down ~1.5-2% but crop output expected to vary 3-5%.
items.quote: As of now, as of September, compared to June, our gross NPA on agri has remained largely constant. We've not seen any signs of concern or deterioration. It has held steady.

items.statement: Revised FY27 zinc cost of production guidance downward to $825–$850/ton from prior $975–$1,000/ton
items.quote: we are revising our COP guidance to $825 to $850 for the full year.

items.statement: Confident of FY27 silver production guidance of 680 tons (H1: 340 tons sold)
items.quote: we are confident we will be able to deliver our guidance of 680. And if you see, in the H1, we have sold 20 KT of concentrate, which includes 20 ton of silver as well. So, put together, we have done 340, you can assume, in H1.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 capex: INR1,200 crore (sustaining) + INR700 crore (growth)
items.quote: During the quarter, we have spent around INR1,200 crore s on sustaining capex and around INR700 crores on the growth capex

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance: INR5,000 crore (sustaining + growth)
items.quote: So, w hole-year outlook, we are on the same line, the way we have guided , t he whole -year outlook is in the range of INR5,000 crores only

items.statement: Silver deficit projected at 1.44K tons in 2026 (6th consecutive year)
items.quote: Silver, again, is expected to remain in deficit for the sixth consecutive year in 2026. The overall shortfall is projected at about 1.44 thousand tons.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 zinc COP: $703/ton (29% better YoY)
items.quote: Our zinc cost of production in second quarter FY27 stands at $703 per ton. Zinc cost of production, we had guided earlier will be for the year we had guided for a projection of $975 to $1,000.

items.statement: Silver production contributed ~45% to H1 FY27 profitability (Q2: 173 tons, +20% YoY)
items.quote: saleable silver production has risen 20% year-on-year. This stands at 173 tons in this quarter. This has contributed approximately 45% of first-half profitability.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 lead concentrate sale: 10 KT (10 ton silver + 6,000 ton lead), INR300 crore revenue, INR155 crore profit
items.value: INR300 crore revenue, INR155 crore profit
items.quote: we have sold 10 KT of concentrate, which consists of 10 ton of silver and 6,000 ton s of lead. Overall revenue generated is INR300 crores, and out of this, profits created INR155 crores

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, energy/currency volatility may drive near-term market volatility
items.quote: The global business environment remains challenging amid escalating geopolitical tensions, energy and trade disruptions, changing tariff policies, and divergent regional growth trends.

items.statement: Exploration for 4 critical mineral blocks (3 exploration, 1 mining lease) to conclude by Q3 FY29
items.quote: we have a guidance of -- we'll be finishing our exploration program in the third quarter of FY29. So, that will be the time when we will know the exact ore body position and resources available there.

items.statement: Renewable energy usage: 27% in Q2 FY27 (target: 35% in coming quarters); HZAPL subsidiary at 100% renewable power
items.quote: In this quarter, the renewable energy accounted for 27% of our power consumption, which we intend to take to 35% in the quarters to come. In one of our subsidiaries, HZAPL, Hindustan Zinc Alloys Private Limited, I'm happy to report that that subsidiary is using 100% renewable power now.

items.statement: NIM to decline marginally in Q3 FY27 due to FCNR(B) impact, then stabilize and rise with current policy rates
items.quote: We do expect a marginal decline in NIM in the current quarter. But after that, we do expect NIM to start increasing even at the current policy rate levels.

items.statement: Expect 2 more repo rate hikes (25bps each) to 6%, with deposit repricing following gradually
items.quote: We do expect more repo rate hikes to happen. Our house view is that there will probably be two more rate hikes. RBI has been doing it in the context of managing inflation as well as financial stability and balancing growth.

items.statement: FCNR(B) deposits ($18B) to be deployed over next 2 quarters; bulk deposits reduced using FCNR funds
items.quote: in many areas, including what you really mentioned. We have deployed this in paying off some bulk deposits. Some of this has gotten deployed in the loan growth which has happened during the quarter. The other balance, we would deploy it over the next two quarters

items.statement: No specific capex guidance provided; focus on operational resilience and digital capabilities
items.quote: Maintaining high standards of governance, deepening coverage and enhancing delivery capabilities with a focus on simplicity and operational resilience, are key drivers for our risk-calibrated profitable growth.

items.statement: Loan book grew 30% YoY (24% excluding FCNR leverage); corporate loans up 30.6% YoY
items.quote: total loan portfolio grew by 30% year -on-year and 12.3% sequentially, compared to 19.6% year-on-year and 5% sequentially, in the last quarter. Excluding leverage on FCNR (B) deposits, the total loan portfolio also grew by 24% year-on-year

items.statement: Corporate loan growth broad-based (capex, working capital); demand shift from bonds/ECBs to bank borrowing
items.quote: The growth has been largely broad-based, and it includes segments across capex, and a higher working capital cycle. Yes, there has been some demand shift from bond market, ECBs, towards bank borrowing.

items.statement: FCNR(B) impact on NIM estimated at 9-10bps; CASA ratio decline contributed to margin compression
items.quote: The impact of that mix change between CASA and term deposits has been about nine to ten basis points.

items.statement: FCNR(B) landed cost ~6.5% (including hedging); exempt from SLR/CRR/PSL
items.quote: comes to about 6.5%, that includes hedging and everything else on FCNR (B). It is an important source of growth. In addition, as we did mention, that FCNR (B) is exempt from SLR, CRR and PSL requirements

items.statement: Loan demand strong across retail (mortgage, personal, jewel loans), business banking, and corporate segments
items.quote: Loan growth has picked up over the last three or four quarters across segments. This is largely a reflection of the continuing momentum of economic activity as well as impact from very supportive policy measures by government and RBI.

items.statement: Gross NPA additions ₹4,833cr (₹3,700cr rural/retail, ₹1,100cr corporate); net additions ₹1,213cr
items.quote: We have had a gross addition to NPAs of about ₹4,800 crore during the quarter, out of which rural and retail is ₹3,700 crore, and corporate and business banking is about ₹1,100 crore. Against this ₹4,800 crore of gross addition, there has been recoveries and upgrades of ₹3,600 crore.

items.quote: We have earlier also indicated we will do a 50-bps cut this quarter and probably 50-bps in the next quarter. The marginal cost of borrowing increase is slightly because of the mix of borrowing that we've taken right now.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowing at 9.1% in Q2 FY27, with average cost stable at 9.1%.
items.quote: Our marginal cost of borrowing stood at 9.1% in Q2 FY27, while average cost of borrowing was stable at 9.1%.

items.statement: Borrowing cost expected to remain in 9.2%-9.3% range till March FY28, despite ECB and NCD mix.
items.quote: So that's where we are of a view that our borrowing cost will stay in this 9.2% to 9.3% range till March.

items.statement: Customer acquisition momentum expected to accelerate in H2 FY27, targeting >1 Lakh new customers/month (currently ~80K).
items.quote: Ideally, we would like to publish more than 1 Lakh customers every month, and that's the target that we are working on. We are right now around 80,000 customers per month.

items.statement: No significant shift in demand for smaller-ticket loans observed; no specific pattern detected.
items.quote: There is no specific pattern I can relate to.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to inch up in Q3-Q4 FY27 due to drought and festive season, but remain within 3.5%-4% guidance.
items.quote: Right now, what we are saying is that even if we budget a certain amount of increase because of the drought situation, we don't see it go beyond our guidance in this entire year. So right now, if you remove the provisions that is the buffer that we have 45 bps, we are at roughly around 3% credit cost. Including the buffer, we are at around 3.45%. And even if we see an inch in credit cost, we are n

items.statement: Insurance regulation reforms may impact ROA by 25-30 bps; pricing adjustments possible to mitigate impact.
items.quote: The impact we see is around 25 bps to 30 bps on our ROA, which I think we are better placed than anywhere else in case we need to cover it through pricing to protect our ROAs.

items.statement: INR 940 Cr NCDs mobilized via private placement in FY27, supporting ALM strategy.
items.quote: We also mobilized INR 940 Crore of domestic NCDs through private placement process in this financial year.

items.statement: Promoters in active discussions for strategic investor at HoldCo level; progress expected in next 2 quarters.
items.quote: See, as you know, currently, the promoters are in active discussion for a strategic investor as the whole group. That is where it is. And we should see some progress in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 same-store sales growth (SSSG) expected to be >10% to achieve double-digit full-year growth.
items.quote: Q3 will have to be higher than 10%, as you rightly said, for the first nine months to look like double-digit growth.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 SSSG target is double-digit (9% adjusted for festival shift).
items.quote: our goal is to achieve double-digit for the full year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve by ~30 bps annually due to double-digit growth vs. 6-7% cost inflation.
items.quote: our growth would be double digit, whereas our cost inflation at the store level would be 6% to 7%, and that would probably improve our EBITDA margin by 30 bps every year.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth driven by market share gain (not volume increase) due to inflationary pressures.
items.quote: our same-store sales growth is largely because of market share gain, and that is exactly what's happened in quarter 2 also

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance revised upward; H2 expected to outperform H1 but balanced growth targeted.
items.quote: What we have tried this year is that we try, and in H2 -- in the H1 itself, we tried to balance and to bring in maximum possible revenue, so there is not too much of mismatch in H1, H2. I'm sure there might be some marginal difference in H2, but it will not be in those likes of what we have been seeing earlier, hopefully, unless the customers have too much pressure on us.

items.statement: Total capex for greenfield project INR220 crores; INR106 crores spent by Sep '26, balance over next 12 months.
items.quote: The total capex planned for the greenfield project is INR220 crores, of which INR106 crores is spent till 30th September '26, and the balance is expected to be deployed over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Order book at INR760 crores (up from INR400 crores at FY27 start), to be executed over 15-18 months.
items.quote: The order book is expected to be executed over the next 15 to 18 months. The cash conversion cycle stands at 63 days as on 30th September '26 compared to 81 days for the full year ended FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 28.1% (vs. 23.3% in H1 FY26); PAT margin at 18.6% (vs. 13.7%).
items.quote: EBITDA for the period stood at INR55 crores vis-a-vis INR23 crores in the corresponding period of the previous year, translating to a growth of 139% year-on-year. The EBITDA margin improved from 23.3% to 28.1% year-on-year.

items.statement: Margins expected to sustain or improve slightly in H2 FY27 and FY28; no major erosion seen.
items.quote: Yes, our efforts are to make it better and better or at least maintain it. That's our effort and we see there is no otherwise reason for us to worry.

items.statement: Localized production expected to expand margins substantially; import cost savings ~18-20% (duty + freight).
items.quote: The cost saving, the import duty and the freight put together is today, say, 18% to 20%. That definitely goes away, plus the overhead difference, right?

items.statement: Price realization improved due to product mix, volume increase (~40%), and cost efficiency.
items.quote: Product mix and operating leverage, which is a combination of volume increase of close to 40%, better price realization, and cost efficiency measures, were the main contributors to the improved gross profit margins.

items.statement: Strong demand from grid modernization, renewables, data centers, and industrial electrification; order inflow exceeds targets.
items.quote: We are seeing increased order inflow from all sorts of customers in India also and abroad also and that's the reason our numbers are much more than what we were originally targeting.

items.statement: RIP bushings dominate revenue (86% by value, 40% by volume); OIP and high-current bushings contribute 14%.
items.quote: By product category, RIP bushings accounted for 86% of the revenue, while OIP and high-current bushings contributed to 14%. Within the domestic sales, the contribution of the retrofit and services business has doubled from 4% to 8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Product mix shift expected post-export ramp-up (FY28-FY29); localized production to alter landscape.
items.quote: Till now, whatever is happening is as per our trend which we were doing and I believe that from the next year mid, we should be able to start booking export orders and that will probably change the landscape going forward from '28-'29.

items.statement: New entrants in high-voltage RIP bushings announced; competition expected but manageable.
items.quote: There are a couple of companies who have announced that they would also come into bushings, apart from the Hitachi and CG type of customers. So, yes, we are aware that people are wanting to come, or they have announced investments. So, we are okay. We are prepared for that.

items.statement: No supply chain disruptions or material shortages expected in near term; inventories managed well.
items.quote: We don't see any supply chain disruption or any supply chains causing problems in our invoicing for the next couple of months. As of now everything is good to go.

items.statement: INR106 crores raised via equity/allotment (INR91 crores shares + INR15 crores warrants); proceeds for growth/capacity expansion.
items.quote: The proceeds will support the company's growth plan and ongoing capacity expansion initiatives.

items.statement: Greenfield facility to enable INR900-1,000 crore revenue by FY30-FY31; localized 550 kV RIP bushings by mid-FY28.
items.quote: Put together, we see that the Unit 1 and Unit 2 would be able to invoice close to INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores of bushings as a combination of Unit 1 and Unit 2, and a combination of assembly model and the localized model. And by 2030-'31, we expect to fully utilize this potential of both the plants.

items.statement: Localized core production trials encouraging; type testing expected in next few weeks.
items.quote: The initial results of our localized core have been very, very, very encouraging. And we are just keeping our fingers crossed that in next couple of weeks we should be able to send the bushings for type test with satisfactory result.

items.statement: Maintain same revenue run rate of 106% for FY27-FY28; Q3-Q4 typically stronger than Q1-Q2
items.quote: we are planning to and we have a pipeline to maintain the same run rate. But to make better than this requires a lot of extra efforts. But going forward, we keep trying to maintain the same run rate.

items.statement: Q3-Q4 revenue expected to be better than Q1-Q2 due to historical seasonality
items.quote: Quarter 3 and Quarter 4 is better than the Q1 and Q2. Or you can say the first half is always better than the last half too. This is over the last 5 years we have done the same things. So, it will always be a better one.

items.statement: ZeroTouch revenue to contribute 20-22% of topline in next 2 years
items.quote: our expectation in the next 2 years of line from ZeroTouch, we are expecting 20-22% revenue will be contributing by ZeroTouch.

items.statement: International revenue expected in FY27 despite unfavorable market conditions
items.quote: inspirationally, we are expecting this financial year revenue from the international. But you know that current situation of international market is not that much favorable.

items.statement: Order book size of Rs. 78 crores as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: So, as on date, the size number based on 31st, 30th September is Rs. 78 crores.

items.statement: ZeroTouch EBITDA margin expected at 50-60%+ due to proprietary tech
items.quote: More than 50%-60% plus EBITDA margin we have into the ZeroTouch because it is a completely proprietary product.

items.statement: ZeroTouch pricing based on volume of question papers printed
items.quote: we are charging. So, the number of question paper getting printed by our device and delivered, according to that, we charge them.

items.statement: ZeroTouch revenue nominal in H1 FY27; Q3 expected to see significant revenue
items.quote: we have booked revenue... And Q3, we are expecting a good amount of revenues as our exam is already started from this month.

items.statement: International margins initially lower due to marketing/investment costs
items.quote: when you enter into the new field, new areas, initial stage it will be a certain investment into the marketing plus expanding and certain cost is always becoming high.

items.statement: Team size increased from 156 to 178 to expand sales and execution capabilities
items.quote: during this 6 month, we have increased our team size from 156 to 178 that we have increased our entire sales capability and execution team.
